correctness.rationale: For n≥4 the exterior square of the standard real module is the irreducible hook with degree d=(n−1)(n−2)/2. Its full real coefficient space has dimension d² by Schur orthogonality. The character is ((f−1)(f−2))/2−t by the exterior-square trace identity and F(g²)=f+2t. The Fourier projector's row sums in absolute value are d E|χ|, attained by a real sign vector. Averaging over left and right translations fixes the block and yields the unique equivariant projection onto it, since the full real coefficient blocks of S_n are pairwise inequivalent absolutely irreducible S_n×S_n modules. Extending coordinate evaluations by Hahn–Banach proves absolute=relative. Orthogonality to constants gives E|χ|=2 E(−χ)_+; the exact disjoint-cycle probability is r_(n−f−2t)/(f!2^t t!), including r_0=1. For the limit, the finite r_m are bounded by 1 and converge to exp(−3/2); the summable domination by t/(f!2^t t!) justifies the limiting sum directly. The independent replay confirms the rounded constant 0.643322969593223 and the finite formula on all permutations for n=4,…,7.
residual_risks: The finite calculations corroborate the analytic all-n proof; they do not test uniqueness of an optimizer under arbitrary non-equivariant choices.
